rv.q: Ultimately, ‘Groundhog Day’ is a surprisingly profound exploration of how to live a good life by appreciating the wonder and specialness in the everyday: Rob Howell's beautifully detailed set design seems to blossom as Phil's cynicism melts away.
I can’t remember a musical in which I chuckled pretty much the entire way through.
And this playful, profound show is the real deal, too.
Matthew Warchus and Tim Minchin’s musical is a dizzying, blistering and joyous reinvention of Danny Rubin’s cult story.
And only when he repairs his selfish ways will salvation arrive. Minchin and his director, Matthew Warchus, were right to persevere with this show and have used the time well to hone the story.
Matthew Warchus’s production bubbles with mischief and invention and Andy Karl is superb as Phil, managing to be thoroughly obnoxious while also persuading you to root for him.
Sublimely witty and surprisingly profound, it’s a pleasure to experience this new, improved musical version of Groundhog Day again.
Tender, and brutally brilliant.
The big surprise is that it still lifts us with its comedy, and thrills us with its theatrical invention.
Enjoyable it most definitely is.
This is all adazzle but seeing it twice is enough for me.
This fresh run proves once again that the production is a timeless triumph.
That’s what makes Groundhog Day such an enjoyable show: it earns its happy ending, which unfolds with grace and a sense of wonder.
You would be hard-pressed to find a slicker, more stylish and wholly enjoyable piece of theatre in London right now.
Groundhog Day is a deft and delicious delight and that cannot be repeated enough.
Faith in humanity is restored in this delightful show: the hype, for once, is to be believed.
It’s an absurdly droll parable played with verve and boundless energy by cast, musicians and cheerleader dancers who double as local characters.
It’s a bravura performance, bolstered by a strong set of supporting roles.
The showstopper and Groundhog Day’s best number, Hope, is a brilliantly executed ensemble piece about the power of self-acceptance and the pleasure to be found in just being nice to people.
Groundhog Day is a masterpiece!
Minchin, the man who in Matilda gave Dahl the warmth he never had, has done it again with this transmutation...
Laugh-out-loud comedy and high emotion create the perfect blend of philosophical study and fulfilling evening entertainment.

This award-winning production (first seen at the Old Vic in 2016) with book by Danny Rubin, music and lyrics by Tim Minchin and directed by Matthew Warchus (the creatives behind Matilda the Musical) has its own magic to share.
Minchin and Warchus bring an entertaining theatricality and depth to it.
With visually stunning staging, vocal powerhouse performances, Minchin’s earworms, and a plot which captivates throughout – this is a show you could watch on repeat, this is a true work of art.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this "instant classic" musical's return, praising Tim Minchin's witty lyrics, Matthew Warchus's inventive staging, and Andy Karl's galvanizing performance as the cynical weatherman, calling it a joyous, profound triumph.
